KNOW THE BLOCK

How to play

01 / Maze Munch

Use arrow keys, WASD, swipe, or the on-screen arrows. Your next turn is buffered until a corridor opens. Collect every dot (10 points) to clear the maze. Power treats (50 points) make rivals vulnerable for 7 seconds. Catch them for 200, 400, 800, then 1,600 points. Clear a level for 500 extra points. You have 3 lives.

New: DAWG Atelier

My DAWG → Fashion / 3D opens a rotatable 3D showroom. Edit body traits, garments, shoes, accessories, auras, and dyes. Appearance is a sixth trainable attribute; advanced fashion unlocks at 5, 10, 15, 20, and 25. Basic styles are free to equip. Save three looks per character, choose three lighting setups, export a skinned GLB, studio photo, transparent 8-view turntable, or 12-frame run atlas, and rank your kennel by Flex. Existing DAWGs retain their legacy genome. New DAWGs use SHA-256-derived genomes. Cosmetic edits do not change game abilities.

Your permanent DAWG

Open My DAWG to discover, adopt, name, and train full-body characters. Earn XP when a run ends, then spend training points. Your active character joins new runs; paused games keep their original character and benefits. Daily Run uses standard rules. Circuit League compares your kennel on this device. Character files and full save backups carry DNA and growth between devices.

New in Living City

Fresh runs generate new maze routes, Cross roads, Snake obstacles, and Flappy skies. After Hours shuffles four story setups, cast members, locations, clues, soundchecks, and epilogues. Authored story pieces can recur; the Daily Run intentionally keeps its layout for the day. Resuming a save preserves its world.

Dash: press Shift, E, or the Dash button for a 0.68-second shielded speed burst. It recharges in 6 seconds of active play. Gold bags: a timed loot bag appears after 80 and 160 pickups per maze; collect it within 12 seconds for 500 points on level one, increasing by 100 per level. The timer freezes while paused.

Districts: each cleared maze moves you to another district, with new colors, additional routes, and faster rivals. Street rep: pickups, rival catches, loot, level clears, and profitable trading runs unlock cosmetic palettes. Progress saves on this device. Focus view expands the arcade; press Escape or use the exit button to leave.

Made for your thumbs

On a phone or tablet, Play opens a dedicated screen fitted around the maze and controls. Drag the joystick to steer, or choose the D-pad in Settings. Swipe on the maze also works. Use your other thumb to dash. Left-handed layouts, optional vibration, and lighter effects are available. Rotate to landscape for controls beside the maze. Return to the arcade to pause your run; Play resumes it after a countdown.

Daily Run

A new seeded 60-second challenge appears each local calendar day. Everyone using the same date gets the same starting layout and rule variation. Earn bronze at 800 points, silver at 1,600, or gold at 2,800. Medal rewards grant 100, 150, and 250 street rep once per medal per day. Replays can improve your daily personal best without claiming the same reward again. Scores are personal records on this device.

02 / 60-Second Rush

Get the highest score in 60 seconds of active play. Hits cost 150 points and reset positions, but don't end the run. Clear a maze to keep scoring on the next one. Pause freezes the clock.

Street Hustle

Start with $1,800 cash, a $2,500 debt, and 30 bag slots. Buy fictional goods where they're cheap and sell where they're expensive. Each trip takes one night, changes prices, and adds 3% interest to debt. Price arrows compare with each good's base value, not a guaranteed sale price. Stock in your bag also shows its average purchase cost and current gain or loss per unit. Sell all stock liquidates your bag without ending the run.

Every district has finite stock and connected prices. Rival traders move stock each night; events and weather affect markets. Contact orders pay a fixed reward if delivered before the deadline. Ask the street wire once each night for current prices elsewhere; they may move before you arrive. Travel may trigger an encounter with explicit choices. Resolve it before trading or traveling again. Trading raises heat and encounter risk. The safe protects cash and earns 0.5% per night; withdraw to spend it. Buy up to 90 bag slots. On night 30, sell or cash out. Cashing out sells all goods at current prices, withdraws savings, and pays debt. Your final score is net worth, which can be negative.

Flappy DAWG

Tap the sky or the FLAP button to fly. On a keyboard, use Space or Up. Each cleared tower earns 10 points; crossing near the center earns 5 extra. Avoid towers, the floor, and the ceiling. Bronze: 50, silver: 150, gold: 300.

DAWG Cross

Tap to hop forward, swipe to steer, or use the direction buttons / WASD. Dodge traffic and ride floating decks across the canal. New rows earn 10 points and gold earns 25. Parks appear every five rows. Move at least once every 15 seconds. Bronze: 100, silver: 300, gold: 600.

DAWG Dash

Swipe left/right to change lanes, up to jump crates, and down to slide under arches. On a keyboard use arrows or WASD; Space also jumps. Tall roadblocks require a lane change. Every row has a clear lane. Gold gives 25 points; distance gives 1 point per meter. A diamond shield absorbs one hit; the U-shaped magnet collects gold across all lanes for 10 active seconds. Power-ups appear in the clear lane. Bronze: 400, silver: 1,200, gold: 2,500. Pausing freezes the run and power timers.

Arcade passport

Earn a stamp by reaching each game’s target in a completed run. Every stamp grants 100 rep once; all nine add 300 more. There is no expiry or streak to maintain. Existing records count and the passport travels with save backups.

Neon Snake

Swipe or use arrow keys / WASD to turn. Collect gold for 25 points and grow your pack. Avoid the walls, stone obstacles, and your tail. Reverse turns are blocked, and one turn can be queued per step. The pace rises with each pickup. Bronze: 100, silver: 300, gold: 600.

After Hours: New nights, new stories

Explore five places, talk to the locals, and tap pocket items to use them in your current location. Follow the objectives and episode clues to reach the rooftop. The optional lost-badge favor changes your epilogue and adds 150 points. There are three endings. Hints are always free; progress and discovered endings save on this device.

Progress: Street Hustle saves after each action. Arcade records save when a run ends. Your maze run stays saved when visiting other games. Switching between maze challenges replaces that maze run after confirmation. Space or P pauses; leaving the tab pauses automatically.

      Your rotation.

      3 SAVED OUTFITS / CHARACTER
      MEET YOUR NEXT MAIN CHARACTER

      Different by DNA.
      Legendary by play.

      Coats, fits, headwear, glasses, accessories, colors, body shapes, and signature crests combine into a vast procedural collection.

      Each new identity starts with 128 secure random bits; domain-separated SHA-256 derives a versioned genome. Duplicate imports are rejected. Visual similarities remain possible; finite traits cannot promise infinite unique appearances.

      Rarity is cosmetic. Every DAWG starts with the same total attribute points and can reach level 50. No wallet, purchase, token, or resale value is involved. Your kennel holds 24 characters.

      YOUR KENNEL / THIS DEVICE

      The circuit league.

      Compare your real saved characters by Circuit Points, level, or Flex. Appearance training, equipped fashion tiers, palette harmony, mastery, and saved outfits build Flex. This league is local to your device.

      How rankings and growth work

      Flex is a separate 0–1,000 fashion score: Appearance × 10, equipped item tier totals × 3, palette harmony × 1.5, 5 per mastery badge, and 10 per saved outfit. It grants no extra game score. Each game contributes up to 1,000 circuit points from that character’s best completed score, for 9,000 total. Targets: Maze 5,000; Rush 3,000; Daily 3,000; Hustle $20,000 net worth; Flappy 300; Cross 600; Snake 600; Dash 2,500; After Hours 1,200. Replaying improves a best; it does not stack leaderboard points.

      Ranks: New Blood → Street Regular at 1,000 → Circuit Pro at 3,000 → Night Legend at 6,000 → Hall of Fame at 8,500. Circuit ties use lifetime XP, then DNA. Career benefits are allowed; Daily always stays standard.

      Positive completed runs earn 20–200 base XP, scaled to each game’s target. The first score at 25% of a target adds 75 XP once per game. Story XP can grow with Charm. Hustles must last at least 3 nights to earn XP. Zero-score runs earn none. Level 50 is the cap; careers have no expiry, paid boosts, or login streaks.

      These are device-local, editable saves, not verified online results. Sharing a character file copies it. A future online competition needs server-backed identity, verified results, and its own fair-play rules.
